# One workflow for every dataset

Follow each example from Define to Write. Use `synthetic`, `zeisel` or `your-study` consistently as the dataset name. Read the page before copying its command.

| Step | Your decision or output |
|---|---|
| Define | One answerable question and the unit of observation |
| Preview | Understand the plots and output locations |
| Meet | Trace matrix rows and columns to metadata and provenance |
| Check | Validate counts and identifiers; inspect sample/donor mapping |
| Run | Generate QC, normalized expression and exploratory PCA |
| Verify and Explain | Recalculate a cell and explain what the figures support |
| Write | Create a short report with results, checks and limitations |

## Find your outputs

| File | Location inside `results/DATASET/` |
|---|---|
| QC and PCA plots | `figures/qc.png`, `figures/pca.png` |
| All-cell QC decisions | `tables/cell-qc.tsv` |
| PCA scores and variance fractions | `tables/pca.tsv`, `tables/pca-variance.tsv` |
| Selected genes and their variance | `tables/selected-genes.tsv` |
| QC cutoffs and input checksums | `tables/parameters.tsv`, `tables/input-checksums.tsv` |
| Transformed expression object | `normalized.rds` |
| R and package versions | `session-info.txt` |

`DATASET` means the dataset name; replace it with `synthetic`, `zeisel` or `your-study`. All folders are created automatically by the workflow.

Run commands one at a time. Continue only after success. Recreate inputs only when needed; after changing inputs or QC cutoffs, rerun Check, Run and Verify before interpreting results. The verifier detects changed input bytes. A successful command checks calculation, not scientific interpretation.

Keep learner-generated reports in the ignored `reports/` folder. [Write the report](02-write-the-report.qmd) explains how to create one without adding it to the book.

## Three habits to carry through every example

**Keep decisions separate from calculations.** The script applies your cutoffs; you justify them. It calculates PCA; you decide what the design and metadata allow you to say about it.

**Keep inputs, results and writing distinct.** Raw files belong in `data/DATASET/`, generated outputs in `results/DATASET/` and learner writing in `reports/`. A report should identify the run it describes. Rerunning the script does not rewrite your report's prose.

**Use AI at a specific point.** First make your own prediction or observation. Then ask AI to explain a command or question a claim using supplied evidence. Finally compare its response with the actual files and revise your own explanation. Share only data you are permitted to disclose; do not send participant identifiers.

At each step, keep a brief note of what you did, what you observed and what remains uncertain. Those notes become the Methods, Results and Limitations sections of the report.
